# Rust Coding Standards

## Error Handling

- **Fail fast** — return errors at the earliest detection point; propagate with the **`?` operator**
- Use **`Result<T, E>`** consistently for all fallible operations
- **Avoid `.unwrap()`** and `.expect()` except in tests and provably-safe initialization
- Use **`#[must_use]`** on functions returning `Result` or important values to prevent silent discard
- Define **domain-specific error enums** with `thiserror` for library code
- Use **`anyhow`** for application-level error aggregation with context
- Add context to errors with `.context("description")` or `.map_err(|e| ...)` — never lose the cause chain

## Preferred Patterns

- Prefer **borrowing** (`&T`, `&mut T`) over cloning — zero-copy by default
- Use **`impl Trait`** in argument position for flexible, static-dispatch APIs
- Prefer **iterators** and **combinators** (`.map`, `.filter`, `.collect`) over manual loops
- Use **`enum`** with data variants for state machines and discriminated unions
- Prefer **`Option<T>`** over sentinel values (null, -1, empty string)
- Use **`derive` macros** for `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq` — avoid manual impls unless needed
- Prefer **`&str`** over `String` in function parameters when ownership is not required
- Use **`Cow<'_, str>`** when a function may or may not need to allocate
- Prefer **module-level organization** — keep `mod.rs` thin, push logic into named files

## Avoided Patterns

- **Never `.unwrap()`** in production code paths — handle the error or propagate with `?`
- Avoid **`unsafe`** unless absolutely necessary — document invariants and wrap in safe abstractions
- Avoid **`clone()` in hot paths** — restructure ownership or use references
- Avoid **`Box<dyn Trait>`** when static dispatch (`impl Trait` or generics) suffices
- Avoid **`String` parameters** when `&str` would work — accept the broadest useful type
- Avoid **`Arc<Mutex<T>>`** as a default sharing pattern — prefer channels or lock-free structures
- Avoid **deeply nested generics** — use type aliases to improve readability
- Avoid **`println!` for logging** — use `tracing` or `log` crate

## Performance

- Prefer **zero-copy** parsing and data handling — use `&[u8]`, `&str`, and borrowed slices
- Use **`rayon`** for data-parallel computation when work per item justifies the overhead
- Prefer **`SmallVec`** or **`ArrayVec`** for small, bounded collections to avoid heap allocation
- Use **`#[inline]`** judiciously — only on small, hot, cross-crate functions; let the compiler decide otherwise
- Prefer **`Vec::with_capacity`** when the size is known or estimable
- Use **`criterion`** for benchmarking — measure before optimizing
- Prefer **stack allocation** over heap allocation in tight loops
- Use **`bytes::Bytes`** for reference-counted, zero-copy buffer sharing in IO code

## Concurrency and Atomicity

- Prefer **lock-free** patterns: channels (`crossbeam`, `tokio::sync::mpsc`), atomics (`AtomicUsize`, etc.)
- Use **`rayon`** for parallel iterators over shared-nothing data
- Prefer **`tokio`** or **`async-std`** for IO-bound concurrency with async/await
- Avoid **`Arc<Mutex<T>>`** when a channel or atomic operation would suffice
- Use **`RwLock`** over `Mutex` only when read-heavy access is proven by profiling
- Collect mutations and apply atomically — avoid partial state visible to concurrent readers
- Use **optimistic concurrency** patterns (compare-and-swap via `AtomicPtr`, etc.) over lock-based transactions

## Write Patterns

- For atomic file writes, write to a temp file then **`std::fs::rename`** into place
- For long-running processes, save checkpoints idempotently so restarts resume cleanly
- Prefer **streaming** with `Read`/`Write` traits over buffering entire payloads in memory
- Use **`Drop`** implementations to guarantee cleanup of resources on all code paths
- Prefer **`BufWriter`** for batched IO — avoid many small write syscalls
